title: Equal value and capacity certify a maximum flow and a minimum cut
statement: Let $N$ be a network with single source $x$ and single sink $y$, let $f$ be a flow in $N$, and let $(S, \bar S)$ be a cut of $N$, so that $x \in S$ and $y \notin S$. If the value of the flow equals the capacity of the cut, $\mathrm{val}(f) = \mathrm{cap}(S)$, then $f$ is a maximum flow in $N$ and $(S,\bar S)$ is a minimum cut in $N$.
hypotheses_covered: N is a network (single source x, single sink y)
f is a flow in N
(S, S-bar) is a cut: x in S and y not in S
replaced:
\emph{Let \texttt{f} be a flow and \texttt{K} a cut such that
\texttt{val f = cap K}.  Then \texttt{f} is a maximum flow and \texttt{K} is a minimum cut.}
